title: HOPA - Honest, Open, Proud for Adolescents with mental illness: confirmatory randomized controlled trial
summary:
Mental disorders among adolescents as well as stigma and discrimination associated with these conditions are a burden for those affected and their environment. Due to wide-spread stigma, adolescents face the difficult decision whether they should disclose their illness to others or keep it secret. The Honest, Open, Proud (HOP) program should help adolescents in making this decision. A first pilot study on HOP for adolescents with mental illness yielded promising results: participants showed benefits in terms of reduced stigma stress and self-stigma as well as increased quality of life (QoL) and more positive attitudes to help-seeking (Mulfinger et al., 2018). 

The present study aims to confirm the efficacy of the HOP program for adolescents with mental illness in terms of reducing stigma-related stress and improving quality of life (aim 1), to test whether this effect is stable over time (aim 2), to assess HOP's cost-effectivenss (aim 3), and to identify facilitators and barriers to HOP's implementation (aim 4). We will recruit 238 participants aged 14-21 years with a mental disorder from inpatient, day clinic, or outpatient settings, from 6 study sites in Germany (Ulm, Neuruppin, Rostock, Mannheim, Ravensburg, Augsburg). Participants will be either assigned to the peer-led HOP program or receive psychoeduation as an active control group. Outcomes will be assessed before the program (T0), after the third session (three weeks after T0), after the booster-session (6 weeks after T0), the first follow-up (30 weeks after T0), as well as the second follow-up (56 weeks after T0).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- at least one current mental disorder according to ICD-10 
- current inpatient, day clinic or outpatient child/adolescent psychiatric or psychotherapeutic treatment
- age 14-21 years
- ability to give written informed consent
- written informed consent of parents or legal guardians
- sufficient German language skills (required for group participation and self-report measures)
Exclusion criteria:
- Diagnosis that is limited to substance-use disorder (ICD-10: F1) without non-substance-related current psychiatric comorbidity
- intellectual disability (IQ < 70; ICD-10: F7)
- organic disorder (ICD-10: F0)
- acute psychotic symptoms or acute suicidality
- previous participation in the HOP program
